Four mourners, including two children, have died after a passenger boat conveying people to a burial ceremony capsized in the Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State. Twenty-four other passengers were rescued from the incident, which occurred at about 11am on Friday near the river junction between Oweikorogha and Otuan communities. The Bayelsa State Police Command said the boat was travelling from Ayama to Ukubie community when it reportedly developed a mechanical fault and capsized. The Police Public Relations Officer, Musa Mohammed, disclosed this in a statement on Friday. He said the bodies had been deposited at the mortuary of the Federal Medical Centre, Yenagoa. According to him, 19 rescued passengers were taken to Ayama Clinic, while five others who sustained varying degrees of injuries were conveyed to Family Care Hospital, Yenagoa. Other survivors had returned to their respective communities. The police said the boat operator, identified simply as Omovie, fled the scene, while the boat manager, identified as MV Bina, was taken into custody for investigation. He added that some passengers reportedly urged the operator to steer towards the riverbank after the fault developed, but he allegedly refused and continued sailing before the boat capsized. “The circumstances surrounding the incident are being investigated,” the police spokesman said. Four dead, 24 rescued in Bayelsa boat accident – Police Boat conveying mourners capsizes in Bayelsa, many feared missing In Bayelsa, Diri’s roads can obstruct The Commissioner of Police, Ajao Adewale, was said to have directed the State Marine Police Section to join the search and rescue operation immediately after the incident. Saturday PUNCH gathered that the Divisional Police Officer, Oporoma Division, was also coordinating efforts with local divers and other emergency responders to account for everyone on board. The police said investigations would establish the circumstances surrounding the accident and determine possible liabilities. Earlier accounts from the affected communities had suggested that more than 30 people were feared dead, with others reportedly missing. However, the figures could not be independently verified, while the police confirmed four deaths and 24 rescued passengers in its Friday statement. A community source, who reportedly witnessed the loading of the boat at the jetty, said some passengers had expressed concerns about the number of people on board. The source claimed that some passengers suggested stopping at Oweikorogha to reduce the number of people travelling because of alleged overcrowding, but the proposal was ignored. The former Chairman of the Maritime Union Workers in Bayelsa State, Ipigansi Ogoniba, also confirmed receiving information about the incident but said he was yet to establish the actual number of casualties. The Commissioner of Police expressed condolences to Governor Douye Diri and the families of the deceased, while wishing the injured survivors a speedy recovery. The command warned boat operators against violating maritime safety regulations, particularly overloading and failure to provide life jackets. It also urged passengers to ensure that life jackets were available and properly worn before embarking on water journeys. LInus Effiong
